questions.q: What are the two defining features of a line segment that make it different from a line?
questions.a: A line segment has two fixed endpoints and a definite length. A wrong answer like "it is a line" shows the student hasn't grasped that a line segment is finite while a line is infinite.

questions.q: If I draw two dots on a page, how many lines can I draw that pass through both of them?
questions.a: Exactly one. A student who says "many" is confusing a single point (through which infinite lines pass) with two points (which determine one unique line).

questions.q: Draw a line segment AB and then extend it in both directions. What is the new name for your figure?
questions.a: It is now called Line AB or line $l$. If a student just labels it AB, they miss the concept that the name changes once it extends infinitely.

questions.q: Why do we say a line has no width, even though when we draw it with a pencil, it clearly has thickness?
questions.a: In geometry, we define a line as an ideal concept with length but no width; the pencil mark is just a model. Students who argue about the pencil thickness are focusing on the physical tool rather than the mathematical concept.

questions.q: Can a line be named using only one point? Justify your answer.
questions.a: No, a line requires two points to be uniquely defined, or a single letter like $l$. A student saying "yes" hasn't understood that one point is not enough to show the direction or position of an infinite line.

questions.q: Create a drawing with three points (A, B, and C) that are not on the same line, and connect them to form three different line segments.
questions.a: The student should draw a triangle-like shape with segments AB, BC, and CA. An incorrect drawing shows a failure to connect specific points to form segments.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: A point is a precise location in space ______ by a dot, a line segment is the shortest path between two fixed endpoints, and a line is a collection of points that extends infinitely in two opposite directions.

Fill in the blank: Start by drawing a dot on your paper—that is your "Point." Now, take a pencil and draw the ______ path between two dots using a ruler; that is your "Line Segment" because it has two clear ends.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to visually distinguish and correctly name points, lines, and line segments, and demonstrate the difference between them by drawing and labeling them on paper.
